courses.title: Jobsite Safety Orientation
courses.description: An essential orientation to workplace safety, identifying common jobsite hazards and personal protective measures.

lessons.title: Understanding Workplace Hazards
lessons.objective: Identify and classify common workplace hazards according to OSHA standards.

questions.q: What is the most common cause of jobsite injuries?
questions.a: Falls

questions.q: When must PPE be worn?
questions.a: Whenever there is potential exposure to hazards

lessons.title: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
lessons.objective: Select and use appropriate PPE for different jobsite conditions.

questions.q: Name two types of PPE for respiratory protection.
questions.a: Dust masks and respirators

courses.title: Concrete Basics: Volume & Mix
courses.description: Learn how to calculate concrete volume, account for waste, and select proper mix types for site conditions.

lessons.title: Volume Calculation Fundamentals
lessons.objective: Apply geometric formulas to determine total cubic yardage.

questions.q: What is the formula for cubic volume?
questions.a: Length × Width × Height

lessons.title: Mix Ratios and Adjustments
lessons.objective: Identify standard mix ratios and when to adjust for conditions.

questions.q: What is a standard mix ratio for general concrete?
questions.a: 1:2:3 (cement:sand:aggregate)

courses.title: OSHA Hazard Communication
courses.description: Covers OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard, GHS labeling, and Safety Data Sheet interpretation.

lessons.title: Hazard Communication Basics
lessons.objective: Explain the purpose and structure of OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard.

questions.q: What does GHS stand for?
questions.a: Globally Harmonized System

lessons.title: Reading Safety Data Sheets (SDS)
lessons.objective: Interpret key sections of an SDS to identify risks and precautions.

questions.q: What section of an SDS covers first aid measures?
questions.a: Section 4

courses.title: Supervisor Communication Skills
courses.description: Develop strong interpersonal and leadership communication skills for effective team management.

lessons.title: Active Listening & Feedback
lessons.objective: Demonstrate effective active listening and constructive feedback in jobsite settings.

questions.q: What is one technique to ensure you understand a worker's concern?
questions.a: Repeat back their statement in your own words

lessons.title: Conflict Resolution
lessons.objective: Apply structured problem-solving to manage workplace disagreements.

questions.q: What's the first step in resolving conflict?
questions.a: Identify the root issue

courses.title: Waste Reduction & Material Recycling
courses.description: Learn how to minimize material waste and improve site sustainability through smart resource management.

lessons.title: Sources of Construction Waste
lessons.objective: Identify key contributors to material waste on job sites.

questions.q: What material is most commonly wasted?
questions.a: Concrete

lessons.title: Recycling Best Practices
lessons.objective: Implement recycling and reuse strategies aligned with EPA guidelines.

questions.q: What is a best practice for managing recyclable materials?
questions.a: Label bins and train staff on proper sorting

courses.title: Understanding Roof Systems — From Deck to Shingle
courses.description: A practical introduction to residential and light‑commercial roof systems, layer by layer. Learn structure, moisture barriers, flashings, coverings, and ventilation with field‑ready terminology and practices.

lessons.title: Roof Anatomy & Terminology
lessons.objective: Identify all major roof components, describe their function, and use correct terminology for estimating and inspection.
lessons.fieldIntegration: Activity: Label layers on a roof cross‑section image (deck, underlayment, flashing, covering, vents).

questions.q: What structural members transfer roof loads to walls and foundations?
questions.a: Rafters or trusses

questions.q: Name two common steep-slope roof shapes.
questions.a: Gable and hip

questions.q: What sheet material is commonly installed over framing before underlayment?
questions.a: Roof deck sheathing such as OSB or plywood

lessons.title: Roof Deck & Underlayment
lessons.objective: Assess deck condition and select/install appropriate underlayment types with correct laps, fastening, and sequencing.
lessons.fieldIntegration: Checklist: Deck condition and underlayment overlaps/fasteners verified on a sample area.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of roof underlayment?
questions.a: Secondary moisture barrier beneath the roof covering

questions.q: List two common underlayment categories.
questions.a: Asphalt-saturated felt and synthetic sheet underlayments

questions.q: What is a typical side-lap for #15 felt on standard slopes (verify local code/manufacturer)?
questions.a: About 2 inches side-lap and about 4 inches end-lap

lessons.title: Flashings and Penetrations
lessons.objective: Differentiate step vs. counter flashing and apply correct sequencing at walls, chimneys, and roof edges to prevent leaks.
lessons.fieldIntegration: Photo audit: Document one penetration and identify primary and counter-flashing elements.

questions.q: How does step flashing differ from counter flashing?
questions.a: Step flashing interleaves with each shingle course; counter flashing covers/overlaps the step flashing and is anchored to the vertical surface.

questions.q: Where is drip edge installed relative to underlayment at eaves?
questions.a: Drip edge is typically below the underlayment at eaves and above at rakes; verify local code and manufacturer guidance.

lessons.title: Roof Coverings (Shingles & Alternatives)
lessons.objective: Explain shingle composition, classes, wind ratings, and correct fastening/stagger patterns; recognize alternative materials.
lessons.fieldIntegration: Field check: Verify nailing pattern and exposure on a sample course against manufacturer instructions.

questions.q: What is the function of starter strips at eaves?
questions.a: Provide adhesive bond and correct shingle offset at the roof edge to resist wind uplift and water intrusion.

questions.q: Why is correct nail placement critical on asphalt shingles?
questions.a: To secure through the nailing zone for wind rating and to prevent blow-offs or leaks.

lessons.title: Ventilation & Moisture Control
lessons.objective: Design balanced intake and exhaust ventilation, prevent ice dams, and coordinate insulation and air/vapor control.
lessons.fieldIntegration: Calculator: Intake vs. exhaust net free area (NFA) using manufacturer NFA values.

questions.q: What is a balanced attic ventilation strategy?
questions.a: Providing approximately equal net free area at intake (soffit) and exhaust (ridge/gable) to maintain airflow.

questions.q: Name one method to help prevent ice dams.
questions.a: Continuous soffit-to-ridge ventilation with proper insulation and air sealing; use of ice barrier in cold climates.
